answer: Tile the world: assign each identity one small survey tile, marked by a lone cedar, where it must log wind, meltwater and shade as the zephyr shifts. Neighboring tiles overlap at the edges, so their logs must agree where they meet yet differ inside. A lone honest surveyor fits easily. A sybil operator inventing a glacier of fake tiles must fabricate thousands of edge-consistent, interior-divergent records; every extra alias adds borders that can contradict it, so scale creates its own evidence.
